diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the $\ell_i$ ($i>0$) are all independent, it follows that

issues.failure_explanation: The induction hypothesis is only pairwise independence of r_n from each ℓ_i, and it is never propagated to r_{n+1}. The base case only gives independence of r_n and ℓ_n at the same index. Joint independence of r_n from the vector (ℓ_1,...,ℓ_n), which the product formula for E[L_n] needs, is never shown. Pairwise independence does not give mutual independence.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $r_n$ is independent from $\ell_i$ ($i=1,\dots,n$). The base case is validated by the computations above.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove by induction that r_n is independent of the σ-field generated by (c_0,...,c_{n-1},r_0) through ℓ_1..ℓ_n. This can be done by extending the joint CDF computation conditionally on the past.
issues.overall_effect: The independence of the ℓ_i and the formula E[L_n]=E[ℓ_1]^n are unproved.
issues.title: Mutual independence of the ℓ_i not established by the induction
issues.why_classification: A contained new inductive argument is needed. The conclusion is likely true, but the current proof does not establish it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\mathcal{T}(G_n)$ is a cumulative density function, it is clearly positive and bounded.
Let $\mathcal{T}: X \to Y$ be a positive linear operator preserving linear functions.

issues.failure_explanation: Positivity is argued only for monotone CDFs. For a general G≥0 in B_∘ it fails. Take F a point mass at 1/2 and G the indicator of {1/2}; then (TG)(t)=G(t/2)+G(t/2+1/2)-G(1/2)=-1 for generic t. The dominated-convergence step also uses G(t+(1-t)c)→G(c), which needs continuity of G at c and not only at 0 and 1. So the hypotheses of the cited result are unverified.

failure_location.quote: which implies that $\mathcal{T}$ is continuous at $t=0$ and $t=1$, and thus a positive linear operator from $B_\circ[0,1]$ to $B_\circ[0,1]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish convergence on a suitable invariant cone or space (e.g. monotone/continuous functions) with a convergence theorem valid there.
issues.overall_effect: Convergence of the root distribution to uniform, and every result built on it in Section 3, are unsupported.
issues.title: Operator T is not positive on B_∘ and the continuity argument fails
